title: Minimum kinetic energy
description: Essential Criteria: The student must correctly calculate the minimum kinetic energy as 5 J.

title: Minimum mechanical energy
description: Essential Criteria: The student must correctly calculate the minimum mechanical energy as 17 J.

title: Minimum potential sum
description: Essential Criteria: The student must correctly calculate the minimum sum of gravitational and electric potential energies as -2 J.

title: Resultant force analysis
description: Important Criteria: The student must identify the constant resultant force of gravity and electric force, and find its angle from vertical using tan α = qE/mg.

title: Critical point identification
description: Important Criteria: The student must recognize that the minimum speed/energy occurs at the point where the resultant force points directly toward the center (the 'highest point' relative to the resultant field).

title: Centripetal force application
description: Important Criteria: The student must apply Newton's second law at the critical point: F_resultant = mv²/R, where F_resultant = mg/cos α.

title: Energy conservation setup
description: Important Criteria: The student must use conservation of total energy (kinetic + gravitational potential + electric potential) to relate energies at different points.

title: Potential energy expressions
description: Optional Criteria: The student correctly writes expressions for gravitational potential energy (mgh) and electric potential energy (-qEx) relative to the defined zero point.

title: Sign error in potentials
description: Pitfall Criteria: The student makes a sign error in the electric potential energy term, using +qEx instead of -qEx for the defined zero point.

title: Wrong critical point
description: Pitfall Criteria: The student incorrectly assumes the minimum speed occurs at the top of the vertical circle relative to gravity alone.
